chunks.title: Program overview
chunks.heading: Program overview
chunks.text:
Northstar Patient Support is a fictional program in this demo. It is not a real medicine and not a real clinic.

Northstar arranges home delivery of Northstar capsules for enrolled patients, answers program questions on the nurse line, and writes travel letters when an enrolled patient is away from home for more than three nights.

Northstar is not an emergency service. Trouble breathing, swelling of the face or throat, or a widespread rash is covered in the adverse-event guide. That guide says to call emergency services first.

chunks.title: Eligibility
chunks.heading: Who can enroll
chunks.text:
A patient can enroll only when every point below is true.

- They are 18 or older.
- A prescriber has confirmed moderate or severe Northstar syndrome.
- They are not pregnant and are not planning a pregnancy.
- The prescriber has sent a signed enrollment form.

The patient signs the form. A carer cannot enroll on the patient's behalf. Patients under 18 are not eligible, including when a parent agrees.

chunks.title: Dosing
chunks.heading: How to take Northstar capsules
chunks.text: The usual dose is 40 mg, one capsule, once each morning with food.

chunks.title: Dosing
chunks.heading: Missed dose
chunks.text: If the morning dose is missed and it is still within 6 hours of the usual time, take that capsule with food. If more than 6 hours have passed, skip the missed dose. Do not take two capsules the next morning.

chunks.title: Dosing
chunks.heading: Storage
chunks.text: Keep the bottle closed, below 25°C, and out of sunlight. Do not keep the capsules in a bathroom.

chunks.title: Adverse events
chunks.heading: Mild effects
chunks.text: Nausea in the first week is common. Keep taking the morning capsule. Call the nurse line if the nausea lasts more than three days.

chunks.title: Adverse events
chunks.heading: Urgent effects
chunks.text: Stop the capsule and call emergency services if there is trouble breathing, swelling of the face or throat, or a widespread rash. After emergency care, tell the program within 24 hours on 0800 111 440.

chunks.title: Contact hours
chunks.heading: Nurse line hours
chunks.text:
The nurse line is open on weekdays from 08:00 to 18:00 UK time, and on Saturday from 09:00 to 13:00 UK time. The line is closed on Sunday and on UK bank holidays.

Outside those hours, leave a voicemail. It is returned on the next working morning. The number is 0800 111 440.

chunks.title: Contact hours
chunks.heading: Delivery desk
chunks.text: The delivery desk uses the same hours as the nurse line. A travel letter needs five working days' notice.
